source: Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, ABC News, PAHO

slides.headline: The US just lost its measles-free status
slides.subline: **After 26 years.** The Pan American Health Organization made it official on Nov. 17.
slides.credit: CDC / Cynthia S. Goldsmith / Public domain

slides.body: Since 2025, about [[7,500 people]] in the US have caught measles and **13 have died**. The US had held its elimination status since **2000**. Mexico lost its status too.
Kindergarten MMR vaccination has fallen to **92.4%**. Experts say about [[95%]] is needed to stop measles from spreading. That gap lets outbreaks keep going.
The US must submit a **corrective action plan**, then go [[12 months]] without continuous spread to win the status back. The CDC says it will work toward that.
Officials note the label itself does not protect anyone. **Vaccination does.** Are you surprised measles is back in the headlines? Tell us below.
